reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses precipitation strengthening and hardness improvements in CoCrFeNi HEAs via Nb, Ti, Mo additions, with no mention of Q235 steel, iron oxide films, micro-galvanic corrosion, or hot-corrosion mechanisms. The key premises are entirely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Corrosion protection in Q235 steel is controlled by the uniformity and integrity of the initially formed passive iron oxide film.
Microstructural heterogeneities (inclusions, high grain-boundary density) disrupt the oxide film and create weak spots.
Localized defects in the oxide film lead to accelerated corrosion via micro-galvanic effects.
A more homogeneous oxide layer better inhibits aggressive salt attack at high temperatures (700–900 °C).
Surface treatments (polishing, annealing) can enhance oxide film uniformity and reduce corrosion.
